 GTA 6 DLSS 5 Extended Trailer Experiment Shows What 90 FPS Could Look Like on PC
 The user noted there was “still room for improvement.”
 By   Aritra Bhowmick   
 Updated: Nov. 5, 2026, 4:53 p.m. 
 Related reads: Sony Announces Official Marvel's Wolverine Sales Figure for the First Time, Raises PlayStation Sales Forecast With GTA 6 Imminent 
 Rockstar Games’ upcoming title GTA 6 is yet to receive a confirmed PC release date. However, a user has experimented with footage from the game’s existing extended trailer using Nvidia’s DLSS 5 and Multi-Frame Generation to see how it would look at 90 FPS instead of 30 FPS.
 The experiment was shared by Reddit user u/RevolutionaryBus8208 , who used Veyra 2.1.1 to process the trailer footage. The tool can take video sources, including video files, capture cards, and Remote Play, and apply neural rendering, upscaling, and frame generation in real time.
 Sharing the results, the user noted that DLSS 5 processing latency was relatively low. However, they also highlighted that there was still “room for improvement on certain details.” More like this GTA 6 Rakes in Over $750 Million in Preorders 2 Weeks Ahead of Release Date 
Beyond the DLSS 5 experiment, a recent survey has also highlighted interest in GTA 6 and its online component. Although Rockstar Games has yet to announce an online mode for the game, a survey by research firm Piper Sandler (via Yahoo Tech ) points to strong interest in GTA Online. The survey included approximately 9,000 teenagers, with around 90% of them expressing interest in playing GTA Online.
 In other news, Rockstar Games has announced the preload dates, release times, and file size for GTA 6 .
